implementation: QueryResult.ownedSlice returns an independently retained owner of rows and optional bookmark; slice delegates and releases its owner on return.

createOwnedBookmark pre-admits constructed normalization records, arrays, sorted-key directories and copied operator bytes, invokes the existing normalizer, then uses shared row detachment to own retained nested data.
Slice arguments/result metadata are admitted; adoption failures release independently returned row/bookmark handles.
evidence: Owned bookmarks match legacy normalized values and sorted keys across projection/window/order, multipart and inline/spilled operator fields.
Nested literal byte and operator byte mutations do not affect returned bookmarks; owner remains valid after parent scope disposal.
Exact normalization/output-overlap cap succeeds and cap-minus-one fails, retaining sibling charges; invalid windows release scratch.
Real Parquet owned slices retain independent handles, resume across row groups, survive concurrent admission failure, and release all charges.
Four native R2 jobs at both 64/128 MiB caps retain first and resumed slice owners across cache eviction; releasing resumed outputs preserves first-page charges; final release returns pool to zero.
Existing HTTP range/full-body slice and plain bookmark regression tests remain in the passing regular suite.
boundaries: Input bookmark data must remain immutable during synchronous normalization; retained data uses the existing detachable data contract.
Normalization scratch overlaps detached output intentionally; stricter admission can reject before previously untracked allocation.
Sort/enumerator VM internals are not portable heap measurements.
Small native R2 fixtures prove ownership lifecycle, not production near-cap whole-runtime headroom.
Other audit items and final release gates remain open.
